fullTextSample:
Enrollment closing in 5 days
Enroll Now
AI for Designers and Engineers

A course that teaches you how to use AI to help you build interfaces that people want to use.

Taught by Emil Kowalski

You can tell when an interface was built with AI.

The spacing is slightly off. The animations feel cheap, or there are too many of them. Everything looks like a template. It works, that’s about as good as it gets.

So most of us end up in one of two places. Some avoid AI for UI work altogether, doing everything by hand, others let AI run and accept what comes out, shipping interfaces that feel generic.

Neither one is a good place to be.

AI is only as good as the person directing it

The people getting great results with AI aren’t using a secret model or a magic prompt. They know what a great interface looks like, and they know how to steer AI towards it.

They know how to make AI follow their taste instead of its defaults. When to delegate and when to take over. How to review AI’s output the way a proper designer or engineer would review work, and how to catch the details it gets wrong.

Work that used to take a week takes a day, and the quality bar doesn’t drop, it goes up, because you can spend your time on the things that actually matter.

That’s the skill this course teaches.

“Somewhere along the way, design engineering became about animations and slick demos. In reality, it’s mostly deciding what not to do. Emil gets this. His course is about building great interfaces with AI, not great demos.”

shadcn
Creator of shadcn/ui
What you’ll learn

This is a course about using AI the way it should be used: as a tool that amplifies your taste, not a replacement for it. You’ll learn:

How to encode your taste, or the taste of your team/others, into rules and skills, so AI’s first attempt looks like your work, not a template.
Workflows for building real interfaces with AI, from prototype to polished component.
How to use AI for the parts it’s genuinely good at, and how to recognize the parts where it will let you down.
How to review and refine AI output, so you ship interfaces that feel good.

You’ll also get a set of skills to help you with this process:

Design

/design-foundations

Layouts that feel intentional

/typography

Text people actually want to read

/color

Colors that look right in light and dark mode

/surfaces

All the right ways to use depth

/ui-polish

UI that feels actually finished

/marketing-pages

All you need to build great marketing pages

/design-vocabulary

Ask for exactly what you mean

Engineering

/component-design

Best practices for UI components

/forms-and-inputs

All about building forms, the right way

/touch-and-accessibility

So it works for every user, on every device

/performance

All you need to know to ship fast interfaces

/animations

Motion that feels right

/ui-review

Catch the mistakes before they ship

/engineering-vocabulary

Ask for exactly what you mean

With more skills coming soon.
